title: feat(automation)!: an approval decision resumes a `runAs: 'user'` flow as the person who decided
body:
Part of #24321. This PR delivers what ruling A's letter decides: a `runAs: 'user'` run continues as the decider after an approval decision. The card stays open on one question the measurement raised (see **Open questions**): every HotCRM branch the card names declares `runAs: 'system'`, and item 2 keeps `'system'` flows unchanged.

Clause-②: no (narrowing). A post-decision node that the submitter's rights admitted and the decider's do not is now refused (ruling A item 3). No schema shape moves: `flow.runAs` keeps its two values and only its describe changes.

## What changes (ruling A, comment 6257886738)

- **`@objectstack/service-automation`.** On resume, `resolveDecisionSegmentContext` builds the context the nodes after the pause run with. A `runAs: 'user'` run whose service-stamped signal names a decider (`resumedBy`) continues as the decider. The context is a copy of the persisted one. The trigger user's `positions`, `permissions` and `org_user_ids` are removed, `userId` becomes the decider, and the decider's own grants are resolved by `seedRunGrants`. `seedRunGrants` is the trigger setup's resolver from PR #24495, now shared by both callers. A later pause persists the switched context, so a second decision, a cold resume or a resume with no decider continues from the decider's segment and never falls back to the submitter. `SeededRunContext.triggerUserId` keeps the run's trigger, so the run history (`buildRunTrigger`) still names who started it.
- **`@objectstack/plugin-approvals`.** `decide` hands `resumedBy: actingUserId(context)` to the engine. That is the person the verdict mirror already writes as. The SLA sweep's `SYSTEM_CTX` vouches for nobody, so its auto-decision names no decider and the run keeps its identity. A stranded decision journals its decider, and `continueRestoredRun` replays it as them. The row builders (#24501's region) and the hand-built `{ isSystem: true, userId }` write contexts (#24497's region) are untouched.
- **`@objectstack/spec`** (spec-lane rider, below). The `runAs` describe and comment now carry item 2's sentence. `ResumeSignal` gains `resumedBy`, which is honoured only beside `RESUME_AUTHORITY_SERVICE`. The REST resume body is a closed key set (`inputs`, `variables`, `output`, `branchLabel`), so an HTTP caller cannot send a decider at all, and the marker check is the second wall.
- **Unchanged, by the letter:** `runAs: 'system'` runs (their elevation and the trigger user they carry), flows with no human decision node, SLA auto-decisions, a subflow parent's own nodes (the parent declares no decision node), and the send-back, resubmit and recall doors.

## Measurement (ruling A item 5)

### HotCRM's four branches: who holds the write each post-decision node makes

Read only, `objectstack-ai/hotcrm` at `296167936b06` (pinned to `@objectstack/*` 18.0.0-next.3). Rep = `sales_rep` (`src/sales/profiles/sales-rep.profile.ts`); manager = `sales_manager` (`src/sales/profiles/sales-manager.profile.ts`). Object edit and row policy are the same on every row: the manager holds `crm_opportunity: { allowEdit, viewAllRecords, modifyAllRecords }` (`sales-manager.profile.ts:22`) under the `select` row policy `opportunity_private_owner_only` (`:117`–`:127`, `is_private == false || owner_id == current_user.id`); the rep holds `allowEdit` with `readScope: 'own'` (`sales-rep.profile.ts:52`). Neither set carries a field entry for any column below, so field-level edit is open to both.

| branch | node | field(s) | manager holds it | rep holds it |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `opportunity_approval` approve | `mark_approved` | `approval_status`, `approved_date` | **no**: both `readonly: true` (`opportunity.object.ts:485`, `:498`) | **no**, same |
| `opportunity_status_change_approval` approve | `apply_status` | `stage`, `status_change_approval_status`, `approved_date` | `stage` yes; the other two **no**: `readonly: true` (`:549`, `:498`) | `stage` yes on own deals; the other two **no** |
| `opportunity_status_change_approval` reject | `clear_request` | `status_change_approval_status`, `requested_status` | `requested_status` yes; the verdict **no**: `readonly: true` (`:549`) | `requested_status` yes on own; the verdict **no** |
| `opportunity_qualification_approval` reject | `clear_request` | `qualification_approval_status`, `qualification_requested` | `qualification_requested` yes; the verdict **no**: `readonly: true` (`:215`) | `qualification_requested` yes on own; the verdict **no** |

Every one of these nodes also writes a `readonly: true` column, which objectql strips from every non-system UPDATE (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:15548`, `if (!opCtx.context?.isSystem)`). No permission set can grant such a column; only an elevated write lands it. So **all four branches need elevation**, and all four flows already declare `runAs: 'system'` (`opportunity-approval.flow.ts:57`, `opportunity-status-change-approval.flow.ts:70`, `opportunity-qualification-approval.flow.ts:72`). So do the other two HotCRM approval flows (`account-approval.flow.ts:75`, `lead-conversion-approval.flow.ts:66`). Per item 3 these four are recorded as the pull for a finer elevation: a per-node elevation would let the ordinary fields (`stage`, `requested_status`, `qualification_requested`) go through the manager's own rights while the declared verdict and stamp columns land as platform writes.

**What that means for this PR:** item 2 keeps `'system'` flows unchanged, so this PR changes none of HotCRM's four branches. Their post-decision writes still carry the submitter through the user a system run carries for attribution (#5494; ADR-0073 D2). The in-repo population matches: `showcase_invoice_signoff`, the one example approval flow with a post-decision write, is `runAs: 'system'`, and `showcase_budget_approval`, the one `runAs: 'user'` approval flow, writes nothing after its decisions.

### After the change: attribution, and the run's report when a right is missing

Measured through the real doors, on the harness HotCRM's own suites boot (`@objectstack/verify`'s `bootStack`, `requires: ['automation', 'triggers', 'approvals', 'audit', 'sharing']`), objectstack at `37caa57a7`. The fixture mirrors HotCRM's shapes: a `private` deal object; a rep set (`allowEdit`, `readScope: 'own'`); a manager set (`allowEdit`, `viewAllRecords`, `modifyAllRecords`, with `restricted_note` non-editable); a `record-after-create` flow with a position-routed `approval` node and a post-decision `update_record` on each branch. The rep creates the deal with `POST /api/v1/data/OBJECT`, and the manager decides with `POST /api/v1/approvals/requests/ID/approve` or `/reject`. It was a one-off measurement file, deleted after the run; the permanent pins are listed under Tests.

| flow (`runAs`) | decision | `updated_by` before → after | `sys_audit_log` rows | run | decision door |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `user` | approve | rep → **manager** | `create` by rep; `update {approved_note}` by **manager** | `completed` | 200 |
| `user` | reject | rep → **manager** | `create` by rep; `update {requested_status}` by **manager** | `completed` | 200 |
| `user`, the manager lacks the field | approve | rep → rep (nothing landed) | `create` by rep only | `failed` at `post_approve`: `update_record(OBJECT) failed: [Security] Field write denied: not permitted to edit [restricted_note] on 'OBJECT'` | 500 `RESUME_FAILED`, `repairable: true`, the message naming the request, the run, the node and the denial |
| `system` (control) | approve | rep → rep | `update {approved_note}` by rep | `completed` | 200 |

The submitter's own writes stay theirs (the `create` row and the before-column). A pre-decision flow node keeps the submitter too: the service-automation real-stack test's `submit` node leaves `updated_by` on the rep. A node the decider may not perform is refused loudly and the run reports it. Under the current letter, the `system` row is what HotCRM's four branches still read after this PR.

## Open questions (full four-axis frames in the report on #24321)

1. **Does the switch reach a `runAs: 'system'` run's carried attribution?** Item 2 says `'system'` flows are unchanged. Items 4 and 5 name HotCRM's four branches, and those are all `'system'`. Option A: after a decision, a system run's nodes carry `{ isSystem: true, userId: DECIDER }`. That is the shape the approvals verdict mirror already writes with, and elevation is unchanged. It fixes the four branches, keeps ADR-0073 D2 (posture is not attribution), and keeps the declared parity in `AutomationContext.flowName`'s describe. About 5 lines plus two flipped pins. Option B: keep the letter as this PR does; the four branches stay wrong for good, because they cannot leave `'system'`. **The dev recommends A.**
2. **Do send-back (and its revision-limit auto-reject), resubmit and recall carry their actor too?** This PR implements item 1's "(approve or reject)" literally. No measured flow has a data node on those paths. **The dev recommends keeping the letter until a flow pulls for more.**

## Tests

At `37caa57a7`:
- `packages/services/service-automation/src/resume-decider-identity.integration.test.ts` (new, 14 pins; 933 ms of test time). The data-op envelope after a decision is the decider's resolved grants and none of the submitter's, for approve and reject. A later pause keeps the decider. A second decision moves to its own decider while the run history keeps the trigger. A decider whose grants fail to resolve runs on the baseline. Real stack (ObjectQLPlugin, driver-sql, identity objects, SecurityPlugin, SharingServicePlugin): `updated_by` names the manager after and the rep before; a guard shows the manager's write rests on the manager's own sets; an FLS-denied post-decision node is refused as a repairable strand naming the node and field; the same node with no decider lands as the rep. Controls: `runAs: 'system'`, a decider without the service marker, no decider, and no decision node.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/restored-approval-continuation.test.ts` (one new describe, 4 pins, on the file's existing pinned engine double). On the real engine, `decide` approve and reject run the post-decision nodes as the decider with the decider's grants. The SLA-shaped decision keeps the run's identity. A stranded decision journals `resumedBy: 'u1'`, and `continueRestoredRun` replays as the decider.
- Suites at `37caa57a7` (after merging `origin/main` at `f4755a68a`): `@objectstack/service-automation` `pnpm test` 191 files / 2555 passed; `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` `pnpm test` 81 / 1116 passed; `@objectstack/spec` `pnpm test` 701 / 21311 passed (1 todo). `typecheck` green for all three (`check:test-typecheck` OK, debt ledgers unchanged). The service-automation pin file runs 14/14 in 933 ms of test time.
- `packages/services/service-automation/package.json` gains `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` as a devDependency (lockfile: 3 lines). A `private` object's write verdict belongs to record sharing, so the realistic fixture needs it.

## Ablation (one-off, not kept)

The decider read in `resolveDecisionSegmentContext` was replaced with `undefined` through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1 → 0; blob `7172068a6966` → `6dfa06c97035`). The service-automation tests import the engine relatively, from source, so no build or dist leg applies. The direction was predicted before the run: red on the decider pins. Result: **8 failed / 6 passed**. Failed: the five envelope decider pins, the two real-stack attribution pins, and the refusal pin (without the switch, the rep's set admits the write). Passed: the four controls, the guard and the no-decider control. The tool restored the file (`blob == HEAD 7172068a6966`, `git diff HEAD` empty).

## Gates

Local, at `37caa57a7`, after the final commit: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 127 families over this diff. All 127 were run, each recorded `:: exit 0`. `--ran` reconciliation: **127 derived, 127 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN**. The local-only `check:dev-prereqs` is OK. The first run of the same list, before the last fix, found two reds in this PR's own fixture, both fixed in `bc19d6e1d`: `check:engine-double-contract` (an unpinned data-engine double, now a recording node) and `check:test-source-alias` (`@objectstack/plugin-sharing` was unaliased). It also found three `exit 3` prerequisites (`check:skill-examples`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`), which pass once their builds exist. CI's check-runs were in progress when this PR opened; the seat reads their conclusions.

## Spec-lane rider (declared to the spec lane)

- `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts`: the `runAs` describe and its comment only (item 2's sentence).
- `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`: `ResumeSignal.resumedBy` (new optional member); TSDoc of `AutomationContext.userId` and of the parity sentence under `AutomationContext.flowName`.
- Regenerated by `check:generated --fix` (`gen:docs`, the one artefact it proved stale): `content/docs/references/automation/flow.mdx`, `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx`.

## Acceptance notes

- A strand journalled before this release carries no `resumedBy`, so its repair replay continues as the trigger user. A run that paused before this release and is decided after it does switch. Carrier: none.
- A subflow-hosted approval switches the child run only; the parent continues with its own context. The parent declares no decision node, so this follows item 1's last sentence. Carrier: none.
- No ADR records a ruling on the resumed identity (`docs/adr` searched: ADR-0019, ADR-0044, ADR-0073, ADR-0118). ADR-0073 D2 (posture is not attribution) is the closest, and it is what open question 1 turns on. Per item 6 no ADR line is owed, and none was written.
- `ResumeSignal`, `ApprovalResumeSurface` and `StrandedContinuationSignal` each gain an optional `resumedBy`. That is a published-surface widening beside the declared narrowing; it is named for the seat's re-grade.
